1 رَهِلَ لَحْمُهُ , (S, K,) [aor.
رَهَلَ ,] inf. n. رَهَلٌ, (JK, TA,) His flesh was, or became, quivering, and flaccid, or flabby: (S, K:) and (some say, TA) his flesh was, or became, inflated, or puffy, or swollen, (K, TA,) in any part: (TA:) or it was, or became, swollen without disease; (JK, K, TA;) he being flaccid by reason of fatness, (JK, TA,) and inclining to weakness. (TA.) [See also 5.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
